# Accessibility Standards (WCAG 2.2 AA)

> **Legal Context**: EAA (EU) enforced June 2025 (fines up to €3M). ADA Title II (US) enforced April 2026.
> Accessibility is not optional—it is a legal and ethical requirement.

---

## WCAG 2.2 Quick Reference (POUR Principles)

| Principle | Goal | Key Criteria |
|-----------|------|--------------|
| **Perceivable** | Can users perceive all content? | Alt text, captions, contrast 4.5:1, no info by color alone |
| **Operable** | Can users interact with all controls? | Keyboard accessible, no keyboard traps, focus visible |
| **Understandable** | Is the UI predictable and error-tolerant? | Labels, error descriptions, consistent navigation |
| **Robust** | Does it work with assistive technologies? | Valid HTML, ARIA correct, name/role/value |

---

## Color Contrast Requirements

| Text Type | Minimum Ratio (AA) |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Normal text (< 18px, or < 14px bold) | **4.5:1** |
| Large text (≥ 18px, or ≥ 14px bold) | **3:1** |
| UI components and graphical objects | **3:1** |
| Decorative elements | No requirement |

---

## The 5 Rules of ARIA

1. **Use native HTML first** — prefer `<button>` over `<div role="button">`
2. **Don't override native semantics** — don't add `role="heading"` to a `<button>`
3. **All interactive ARIA roles must be keyboard operable**
4. **Don't hide visible elements** — don't use `aria-hidden="true"` on visible focused elements
5. **All interactive elements must have accessible names**

---

## Anti-Patterns

### S — Semantic HTML (S1–S8)

**S1**: Using `<div>` for interactive elements
```tsx
// BAD
<div onClick={handleClick}>Submit</div>

// GOOD
<button type="button" onClick={handleClick}>Submit</button>
```

**S2**: Missing heading hierarchy — don't skip from `<h1>` to `<h4>`.

**S3**: `<table>` without `<caption>` and `<th scope>` for data tables.

**S4**: Using `<i>` for icon-only buttons without accessible name.
```tsx
// BAD
<button><i className="icon-search" /></button>

// GOOD
<button aria-label="Search players"><SearchIcon aria-hidden="true" /></button>
```

**S5**: Lists using `<div>` instead of `<ul>`/`<ol>`.

**S6**: Missing `lang` attribute on `<html>`.

**S7**: Using `<b>` or `<i>` for semantic emphasis — use `<strong>` or `<em>`.

**S8**: Using placeholder as label replacement in forms.

---

### A — ARIA (A1–A8)

**A1**: `aria-hidden="true"` on focusable elements.
```tsx
// BAD
<button aria-hidden="true">...</button>

// GOOD — either remove aria-hidden, or tabIndex={-1}
<button aria-hidden="true" tabIndex={-1}>...</button>
```

**A2**: Using `role="button"` on `<div>` without `tabIndex={0}` and keyboard handler.

**A3**: `aria-label` and visible label mismatch — screen reader text should start with visible label text.

**A4**: Using `aria-disabled` without `disabled` attribute on native elements.

**A5**: Missing `aria-expanded` on accordion/dropdown triggers.

**A6**: Missing `aria-live` region updates for dynamic content.
```tsx
// GOOD — announce dynamic results
<div role="status" aria-live="polite">{searchResultCount} players found</div>
<div role="alert" aria-live="assertive">{errorMessage}</div>
```

**A7**: `aria-labelledby` pointing to non-existent ID.

**A8**: Using `role="presentation"` on table used for data — only for layout tables.

---

### K — Keyboard Navigation (K1–K7)

**K1**: Removing focus outline without replacement.
```css
/* BAD */
:focus { outline: none; }

/* GOOD */
:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid #2563eb;
  outline-offset: 2px;
  border-radius: 4px;
}
```

**K2**: Custom modal without focus trap — use native `<dialog>` element.
```tsx
// GOOD — native dialog has built-in focus trap
<dialog ref={dialogRef} onClose={handleClose}>
  <button autoFocus>First focusable element</button>
</dialog>
```

**K3**: Missing skip-to-content link.
```tsx
// Add as first element in <body>
<a href="#main-content" className="sr-only focus:not-sr-only focus:fixed focus:top-4 focus:left-4 focus:z-50 focus:px-4 focus:py-2 focus:bg-white focus:text-black">
  Skip to main content
</a>
```

**K4**: Keyboard trap — focus cannot leave a component.

**K5**: Wrong tab order — use logical DOM order, not `tabIndex` values > 0.

**K6**: Custom dropdown/combobox without arrow key navigation.

**K7**: Toast/notifications not dismissible via keyboard.

---

### F — Forms (F1–F6)

**F1**: Input without associated label.
```tsx
// BAD
<input type="text" placeholder="Player name" />

// GOOD
<label htmlFor="player-name">Player name</label>
<input id="player-name" type="text" />
```

**F2**: Error message not associated with field.
```tsx
// GOOD
<input id="email" aria-describedby="email-error" aria-invalid={hasError} />
<p id="email-error" role="alert">{errorMessage}</p>
```

**F3**: Required field without indication — use both `required` attribute and visual asterisk.

**F4**: Form validation only on submit — show inline errors as user types (after first blur).

**F5**: Autocomplete not set on personal data fields (`name`, `email`, `tel`, etc.).

**F6**: Color-only error indication — always add icon or text, not just red border.

---

### V — Visual (V1–V5)

**V1**: Text over complex imagery without contrast layer.

**V2**: `display: none` used for content that should be visible to screen readers — use `.sr-only` pattern instead.

**V3**: Hover-only tooltips not keyboard accessible.

**V4**: Animations without `prefers-reduced-motion` guard.
```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  *, *::before, *::after {
    animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;
    transition-duration: 0.01ms !important;
  }
}
```

**V5**: Focus indicator appears on mouse click but shouldn't — use `:focus-visible` not `:focus`.

---

### D — Media (D1–D4)

**D1**: Video without captions or transcript.
**D2**: Audio content without text alternative.
**D3**: Decorative images not marked with `alt=""`.
**D4**: Complex charts without text description or `<table>` equivalent.

---

## Next.js Specific Patterns

**RX1**: Use `htmlFor` not `for` in JSX labels.

**RX2**: SPA route changes — Next.js 13+ has a built-in route announcer. For custom navigation, manage focus manually:
```tsx
// After route change, move focus to page title or main content
useEffect(() => {
  document.querySelector('h1')?.focus();
}, [pathname]);
```

**RX3**: Fragment component key changes can cause focus loss — assign stable keys to interactive elements.

**RX4**: Injected HTML via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` needs ARIA audit — sanitize with DOMPurify AND check ARIA attributes.

---

## Accessibility Implementation Checklist

### Essential (P0)
- [ ] Every image has `alt` text (or `alt=""` if decorative)
- [ ] All form inputs have associated `<label>` elements
- [ ] Color contrast meets 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text and UI
- [ ] All functionality accessible by keyboard
- [ ] No keyboard traps
- [ ] Focus state visible on all interactive elements

### Important (P1)
- [ ] Skip-to-content link present
- [ ] Heading hierarchy logical (h1 → h2 → h3)
- [ ] `lang` attribute set on `<html>`
- [ ] Dynamic content announced via live regions
- [ ] Error states described in text, not just color
- [ ] `prefers-reduced-motion` respected

### Recommended (P2)
- [ ] ARIA landmarks used (`<main>`, `<nav>`, `<aside>`)
- [ ] Icon buttons have `aria-label`
- [ ] Loading states announced (`aria-busy`, `role="status"`)
- [ ] Focus managed after modal open/close
- [ ] Video content has captions/transcript
